# implement.py parent misclassifies soft-deleted children

## Problem
`implement.py parent <parent-id>` treats a child whose `deletedBy` is set (soft-deleted; `status` remains `open`) as implementable. `_classify_child` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` only checks `status` against `TERMINAL_STATUSES` ({in_review, completed, done, deleted}); it never inspects `deletedBy`. As a result `phase_parent` calls `phase_start` on the soft-deleted child, creates a bogus worktree/branch, claims the item `in_progress`, and stops the chain instead of advancing the parent.

## Reproduction
`wl delete <child>` on a child of an epic sets `deletedBy` but leaves `status: open` (verified with SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X / SA-0MUD5U06J009V0EK, both `deletedBy: plan`). Running `implement.py parent SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0` then started a worktree for SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X and set it `in-progress`, even though both real children were `completed`.

## Expected
A child with `deletedBy` set must be treated as terminal (`skip-terminal`): never claimed, never given a worktree, and never allowed to block parent advancement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_classify_child` treats `deletedBy` (non-empty) as terminal regardless of `status`.
- [ ] `phase_parent` advances a parent whose only non-terminal statuses are soft-deleted children.
- [ ] Soft-deleted children count as terminal when gating in-chain blockers, so a child blocked only by a soft-deleted sibling is still startable (terminal determination must be consistent with `_classify_child`, not status-only).
- [ ] Regression test: a soft-deleted child is skipped and the parent advances.

## Plan: changelog
- 2026-10-07 — plan skill auto-complete path (effort Extra Small / risk Low, approval gate not warranted): added AC3 so the terminal determination used for in-chain blocker gating matches `_classify_child`; traced remaining ACs to the reported bug; no child work items created (below planning threshold).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- None — the pre-check classified this item as below the planning threshold (Extra Small / Low), so no interview questions were asked. Seed intent was taken as authoritative from this work item's description (discovered-from SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0).

## Implementation decisions (implement session)

Implemented as a **single leaf work item** (not decomposed into the 3 plan-slice children). Rationale: issue-type is `feature` with a single cohesive change set (guard + docs + tests) spanning the same files; the operator invoked `/skill:implement` directly and the plan children had not been created. Acceptance criteria are unchanged and all seven are covered.

### Changes
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `_main_checkout_offending_paths()` extracts non-`.worklog/` dirty paths (handles porcelain renames).
  - `_child_main_checkout_violation()` — AC3 guard: child non-terminal + main dirty outside `.worklog/` + worktree clean at parent HEAD → actionable message naming the offending main-checkout paths (mirrors `_worktree_placement_violation` precision, minus the cwd check).
  - `phase_parent` fails closed (`success: False`, `placement_violation: True`, `next_child`) via `_fail_placement` instead of reporting the child for implementation; `phase_drive` propagates it.
  - `_invoke_implement(parse_on_failure=True)` surfaces the parsed failure report so the actionable message reaches `phase_drive` (default `None` sentinel preserved for start/finish callers).
  - `_child_session_env(worktree_path=...)` injects `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` into driven child sessions.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Step 5 and Step 6.1 require verifying the worktree root before the first write and forbid absolute main-checkout edit paths; new guard bullet.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — MANDATORY worktree requirement now states `cwd` is not sufficient and requires root verification before the first edit.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (new) — the `wl`-needs-main-checkout vs edits-need-worktree split and the worktree-safe `wl --worklog-dir <main>/.worklog ...` invocation.
- `README.md` — links the new doc.
- Tests: `tests/test_implement_child_placement_guard.py` (new, AC3/AC4), `tests/test_worktree_isolation_docs.py` (new, AC1/AC5/AC6), plus worktree-root assertions in `tests/test_agents_global_session_per_child.py` and `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py`.

### Assumptions recorded
- Guard semantics: fail closed; no auto-move of the stray changes.
- The `implement.py start` dirty-tree gate means the main checkout was clean when the child started, so main-checkout dirt at guard time is (in practice) the child's — the three-condition check remains precise.
- Orphaned stash `stash@{0}` (no work-item reference: old plan/report test WIP) was acknowledged but **not** deleted — it needs operator triage.
